Developed under the auspices of the NIST Coatings Service Life Prediction Consortium, the NIST 2 m integrating sphere provides a source of collimated ultraviolet radiation in the 290 nm to 400 nm region of the spectrum. Visible and infrared components of the input radiation are largely removed by dichroic mirrors or filters. The physics of integrating spheres ensures that the uniformity of the UV radiation emitted from a sphere exit aperture is ³ 95%. By coupling the integrating sphere with a high intensity UV light source, irradiance levels equivalent to 60 or more "suns" can be achieved at the sphere exit apertures. Adopting a child is a wonderful and exciting event for families. Intercountry (International) Adoption: Tuberculosis May 15, 2024 At a glance U.S. law requires parents who adopt children internationally to have their child screened for tuberculosis (TB). Learn more about TB and the types of tests your child will get during their overseas medical exam. About TB TB is caused by a bacterium called Mycobacterium tuberculosis that spreads through the air from one person to another when a person with TB disease of the lungs or throat coughs, speaks, or sings. The bacteria usually attack the lungs, but TB bacteria can attack any part of the body such as the kidneys, spine, and brain. Keep Reading Tuberculosis in Children TB disease is a serious condition. Worldwide, approximately 1.3 million people died of TB in 2022, including 167,000 people with HIV. In the United States, TB disease is less common than in many other countries. In 2022, the United States reported 8,331 TB cases. Learn more about tuberculosis in the United States at CDC's Tuberculosis Data and Statistics webpage . International Health Regulations Mar. 20, 2026 At a glance International Health Regulations (IHR) provide an overarching legal framework that defines countries mutual obligations in managing public health risks, events, and emergencies that have the potential to cross borders. CDC works with countries around the globe to comply with the IHR by building local capacity to prevent, detect, and respond to health emergencies. Overview The IHR 2005 represents an agreement between 196 countries that have committed to developing and maintaining specific public health capacities that enable them to prevent, detect and respond to public health threats within their borders. Furthermore, when an outbreak or other significant public health event occurs, these countries will report this event under the IHR for the awareness of all countries that are party to the agreement. These outbreaks, or significant events, are considered events of international public health importance. CDC works with countries around the globe to comply with the IHR 2005. Since an IoT product might be defined as including an IoT device and any other product components that are necessary to using the IoT device beyond basic operational features, there are risks that come along with this level of connectivity—especially among so many devices across the globe. We must be able to trust the privacy, security, authenticity, and reliability of these devices, as well as the advanced networks that support them. NIST’s collaborative work across IoT focuses on the role we can play to help guarantee our connected future. pages.description: The crustaceans, non-native and fierce, are taking over the Gulf of Maine. Could eating them help draw down the population?
pages.text: Invasive green crabs: If you can't beat them, eat them. | National Geographic By Kea Krause Photographs by Brian Skerry Published July 11, 2022 • 12 min read West Bath, Maine — If you close your eyes, a green crab scuttling up your forearm feels more spider than sea creature, its little legs picking their way as if spinning silk. If you open your eyes, you will see the forged work of 200 million years: bumpy carapace, plated apron, calcified pincers. The small crabs are exquisite, seemingly carved from jade. The big ones are monstrous looking. They are nimble and chaotic, and likely under any beach rock in the Gulf of Maine. But here, the European green crab is not native. It is an invader , a species that traveled to the region in the 1800s in the ballast water of trading ships. In the centuries since, the crabs have established a thriving population, feasting on soft-shell clams and blue mussels, overtaking fisheries that have sustained Mainers for centuries. Their monstrous appetites and canny ability to adapt and reproduce have outcompeted any efforts to remove them. Green crabs ( Carcinus maenas ) are an invasive species that first appeared in New England waters in the 1800s, mostly likely arriving in the onboard water of large oceangoing vessels. The species’ population has exploded in recent years due to warming seawater temperatures in the Gulf of Maine. Now, one of the last defenses against these marauding creatures is not to eradicate them, but to eat them . What you can get SBICs invest in small businesses through debt, equity, or a combination of both. Debt is a loan an SBIC gives to a business, which the business must pay back, along with any interest. Equity is a share of ownership an SBIC gets in a business in exchange for providing funding. pages.text: Investors sue chip giant Intel after 29% stock plunge Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Investors sue chip giant Intel after 29% stock plunge 7 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Osmond Chia Business reporter Bloomberg via Getty Images Intel boss Tan Lip-Bu Shareholders have sued US chip giant Intel, accusing it of hiding the severity of a slump in personal computer (PC) sales, which they say led to a nearly 29% one-day collapse in the firm's stock. A proposed class action lawsuit in San Jose, California said Intel was too late to alert shareholders about how slowing sales could impact its earnings, allegedly artificially inflating its stock price. Intel shares plunged on 30 October, erasing tens of billions of dollars off its market value the day after it forecasted disappointing revenue in its coming earnings report. pages.text: Itemized deductions, standard deduction | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Itemized deductions, standard deduction More In Help Interactive Tax Assistant Tools Report fraud Tax scams Identity theft Notices and letters Appeals Frequently asked questions Accessibility Contact your local IRS office Contact an international IRS office Tax topics Other languages Top Frequently Asked Questions for Itemized Deductions, Standard Deduction If I must deduct points over the life of my mortgage, and I have a 30-year mortgage, should I divide the points paid by 30 and enter that amount on Schedule A of Form 1040? Answer: No. While you must deduct the points over the life of the loan ratably (equally), you don't divide the points by 30 years. Instead, you divide the points by the number of payments scheduled over the term of the loan (360 monthly payments in the case of a 30-year mortgage) and deduct points each year according to the number of payments you made in that year (less than twelve payments in some cases). If the loan ends prematurely, for example, because you paid it off or refinanced with a different lender, then the remaining points are deductible in that year. Note: This does not apply to loans refinanced with the same lender. Any deductible points not included on Form 1098 (usually not included on the Form when refinancing) should be entered on Schedule A (Form 1040), Itemized Deductions , line 8c "Points not reported to you on Form 1098." He was 86. His death was confirmed in a statement from his family, which noted that "his music was fearless, and so was his spirit." Fearlessness was fundamental in Ulmer's music, which came firmly rooted in the blues but could often sound heat-warped, hallucinatory and feral. These qualities, along with an openness to possibility, endeared him to the free-jazz forefather Ornette Coleman, with whom he started collaborating in the early 1970s. In a statement, the London-born actor said: "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime." pages.description: James Botham is accustomed to working away from the spotlight, but his performance could not be denied against New Zealand.
pages.text: James Botham: Wales' unlikely hero in historic win over New Zealand - BBC Sport Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Image caption, James Botham was man of the match in Wales' historic win over New Zealand By Gareth Rhys Owen BBC Sport Wales Published 16 November 2026 James Botham lay sprawled on the Principality Stadium turf, pain and exhaustion etched across his face. Whenever the whistle blew, the Wales flanker in the red scrum cap took an age to rise. Precious seconds to recover. Nobody counts tackles when the ball is dead. But when play resumed, he was everywhere. Tackling, scrambling, hitting the deck and springing back up. By the final whistle, Botham had helped Wales beat New Zealand for the first time in 73 years. He was man of the match. And as the celebrations began, the tears flowed. Quite an afternoon for a player accustomed to working away from the spotlight. Keeping a Botham out of the headlines was always going to be difficult. His grandfather, Lord Ian Botham , is one of Britain's great sporting celebrities. Outspoken, charismatic and capable of turning cricket matches almost single-handedly, he is box-office. James is different. His game is built on tackles, chasing, wrestling and relentless graft. Few positions in rugby are less glamorous than blind-side flanker. But on Saturday, Wales' number six was the star of the show. James Briones James Briones is the Acting Deputy Assistant Secretary, Grid Upgrades in the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE)'s Office of Electricity (OE), recognized for his leadership and deep expertise in enhancing the reliability and resilience of the nation’s energy systems. In this role, he leads strategic initiatives that strengthen U.S. energy security, affordability, and dominance through innovative investments and modernization, paving the way for a more reliable and resilient energy future. Prior to rejoining the DOE, James served at Amazon Web Services (AWS), where he led global Security Assurance Programs. James brings over a decade of experience from his previous tenure at DOE, where he led cybersecurity R&D efforts to protect critical energy infrastructure. He also spent nine years at the U.S. Air Force’s Space and Missile Systems Center, advancing national defense technologies. He holds degrees in electrical engineering, information systems management, and an MBA, and is certified as a CISSP and GIAC professional. Articles by James Briones

South Korea also says it deployed fighter jets, while Taiwan says it "responded" to Russian military aircraft detected in their respective air defence identification zones. These are unofficial buffer areas beyond territorial airspace where governments identify approaching aircraft for security purposes. Moscow has yet to comment. The alleged incursions are a reminder of Russia's military power ahead of the Apec economic summit in China this week, which Vladimir Putin will attend alongside US President Donald Trump. Japan's Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said the flight paths of the Russian aircraft, off the south-western Okinoshima island, were a "serious infringement of Japan's sovereignty" and "completely unacceptable". The last such incursion was in 2024, when a Russian military patrol plane entered Japanese airspace off Rebun island, Hokkaido. David Madison/Getty Images I had just arrived at Konsen-ji , the third temple on Japan’s Shikoku Pilgrimage route, when a young Japanese girl presented me with two origami cranes. These tiny gifts, I would later learn, symbolized wishes for a safe and smooth journey along the 750-mile circuit connecting 88 Buddhist temples, as well as other sacred sites , on Shikoku, the smallest and least populated of Japan’s four main islands. On my week-long visit to Shikoku, I encountered many acts of kindness, from the innkeeper at Sudachi-an , a local guesthouse in the village of Nabeiwa, driving me to my lodging when I ended up lost in the rain, to a taxi driver insisting that I take a couple of sweet, kiyomi oranges to help sustain me on my day’s trek. This rural Japanese island is a place where history, hospitality and natural beauty converge. Konsen-ji is the third temple on Japan's Shikoku Pilgrimage route. John S Lander/LightRocket via Getty Images The 7,063-square-mile island is the most rustic and remote. DeWitt characterized people of Japanese ancestry during World War II. He insisted that even those who had been born and raised as U.S. citizens nevertheless posed a threat because their Japanese “racial strains” were “undiluted.” Under the authority of President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s Executive Order 9066, DeWitt ordered the removal of all Japanese Americans from the West Coast in 1942. Allowed to take only what they could carry, they were imprisoned, without trial, in some of the most desolate places in the country. Today, the National Park Service preserves those sites so that visitors may learn their story.
